The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of D.Teja who succumbed to injuries on 29.08.2019 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
The deceased D.Teja was working as Cleaner with the respondent No.1 i.e., Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-3611.
Upon the instructions of respondent No.1 the deceased D.Teja was returning from Bhuvaneshwar to V.Kota on 29.08.2019.
While he was on his way at about 10.30 p.m.,. one truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 was moving in front of the respondent No.1 vehicle i.e., vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP- 03-TE-3611.

The truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 has negligently applied brake to his vehicle and has suddenly stopped in the middle of road on Gurapalli Toll gate,
Khallikote, Ganjam District Odisha State.

At that time, the driver of respondent No.1 truck bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-3611 without noticing the negligent act of the truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119, has dashed against said Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 from behind.
Due to the impact of the accident, the deceased D.Teja sustained grievous injuries.

M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
2 3.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to MKCG Medical Hospital and the deceased was succumbed to injuries at about 11.50 p.m., in the hospital.
The petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards transportation, funeral and other expenses.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased D.Teja was very hale and healthy and he was Cleaner.
He was earning Rs.15,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have come to stand still.
The petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have become miserable.
5. The respondent No.1 and 3 are the owners and respondent No.2 and 4 are the insurer vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
6. After registration of the petition.
Notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.3 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.3, the respondent No.3 is placed exparte.

The respondent No.1, 2 and 4 have appeared through its counsels and the respondent No.1 has not filed the written statement,
therefore the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.2 and 4 have filed their separate written statements.
Further denied the petition averments in their written statements.
The specific contention was that, the drivers of both vehicles was not possessing valid driving license on the day of accident.
The insurance policy of the both the vehicles were in force as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.
Further denied the age of the deceased, avocation and income of the said deceased.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
They prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
The respondent No.4 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
8. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased D.Teja died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.08.2019 at about 10.30 p.m., near at Gurapalli Tolgate on V.Kota Bhuvaneshwar Road, Ganjam District, State of Odisha due to the rash and negligence driving of Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP- 03-TE-3611 by its driver?
2. Whether respondent No.2 prove that the driver of Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-3611 drove the same without holding DL?

M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
3 3.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
5.
What order or award?
On perusal of material available on record this court observed that, there is necessary to recast the issue No.1.

Hence, for the reasons issue No.1 recasted as follows:
RECAST ISSUE No.1 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased D.Teja died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.08.2019 at about 10.30 p.m., near at Gurapalli Tolgate on V.Kota Bhuvaneshwar Road, Ganjam District, State of Odisha due to the rash and negligence driving of Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 by its driver?
10.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the Negative,
Recasted Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the Negative.
Issue No.3 : In the affirmative.
Issue No.4

: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.5: As per the final orders for  the following:-
 REASONS ISSUE NO.1 and 2 and RECASTED ISSUE NO.1 :
11.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that the deceased D.Teja was working as Cleaner with the respondent No.1 i.e., Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP- 03-TE-3611.
Upon the instructions of respondent No.1 the deceased D.Teja was returning from Bhuvaneshwar to V.Kota on 29.08.2019.
While he was on his way at about 10.30 p.m.,. one truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF- 7119 was moving in front of the respondent No.1 vehicle i.e., vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-3611.
The truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 has negligently applied brake to his vehicle and has suddenly stopped in the middle of road on Gurapalli Toll gate, Khallikote, Ganjam District Odisha State.

At that time, the driver of respondent No.1 truck bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-3611 without noticing the negligent act of the truck bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119, has dashed against said Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 from behind.
Due to the impact of the accident, the deceased D.Teja sustained grievous injuries.

M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
4 12.
To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Ex . P.1
FIR and
UDR which reveals that one Mano Mohan Rana Bijuli has lodged complaint on 29.08.2019 against the driver of the respondent No.3 offender vehicle i.e., Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119
. Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the seizer mahazar which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.5 and 10 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.4 is the police intimation report.

Ex.P.7 is the charge sheet/final report which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet/final report against the driver of the offender vehicle i.e., Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119.
13.
The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
14. The respondent No.4 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
The RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination the RW.1 has admitted that the offending vehicle Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF- 7119 has valid insurance policy as on the date of the accident.

Further the charge sheet reveals that the Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119 i.e.,
respondent No.3 vehicle was involved the accident and respondent No.4 is the insurer to the said vehicle.
15.

Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondents have admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 and 2 are in the Negative and recasted issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3 16.
The PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that, his deceased son D.Teja was cleaner and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
His son was aged about 18 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being father and sister of the deceased D.Teja were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.
He has further deposed that, he has spent Rs.75,000/- towards funeral and other expenses.
17. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the father of the deceased D.Teja, Petitioner No.2 is the sister of the said deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of himself and petitioner No.2.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased D.Teja.

Since,
M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
5
the respondents have not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
18.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
( i ) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 18 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.8, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 15.03.2001, the accident was occurred on 29.08.2019.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 18 years.
(ii).Income of the deceased:
According to the petitioners deceased D.Teja was Cleaner and he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
In this regard the petitioner has not any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

19. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

entities.text: Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
20.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.14,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year 2019 and thus income of the deceased D.Teja is to be considered at Rs.14,000/- per month.
21. Loss of dependency:
The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

22. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
6 between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged below 40 years and therefore 40% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.5,600/- (14,000 X 40/100 = Rs.5,600).
Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.19,600/- per month (14,000 + 5,600 = Rs.19,600/-).
23. Admittedly, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, Since the deceased was bachelor 50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such 1/2 amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e., Rs.9,800/-.
When the said 1/2 amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.9,800/- (Rs.19,600 - Rs.9,800 = Rs.9,800/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total loss of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.9,800/- X 12 X 18 =Rs.21,16,800/-).
Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.21,16,800/-.

24. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:- In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.75,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25. Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Like wise for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).

M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
7
Loss of consortium: it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence,
in view of the said decisions this tribunal awards under the head of consortium as follows;
(I) Towards filial consortium: the petitioner No.1 and 2 being the father and sister are entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- with an enhancement at the ration of 10% in every three years.

Hence,
petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- each (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40,000/-).
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads.
Sl. No.

Particulars Amount 1. Loss of dependency with Rs. 21,16,800/-
 future prospects 2. Transportation of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
3. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
4. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
5. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 27,500/-
6. Loss of filial consortium Rs. 88,000/-
7.
Medical expenses -NIL-
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.22,81,800/- which is just and proper.

26. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 is the owner and 2 is the insurer of the vehicle in which the deceased was traveling and Ex.P.7 charge sheet/final report does not reveals any information stating that the said respondent No.1 and 2 are held responsible for the occurrence of alleged accident in this case.
Under the circumstances the respondent No.1 and 2 are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Further, the respondent No.3 is the owner and respondent No.4 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.3 and 4 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.4 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.3.
Hence, respondent No.4 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

Accordingly,
I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
27.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
8 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.22,81,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 80:20.
The respondent No.4 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 80% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 20% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of one year.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.2, it is ordered to release the entire amount in their favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected by me and then pronounced in the open court on this the 8th day of October, 2024)
(Gayathri S Kate) XVIII ADDL.JUDGE & ACJM Court of Small Causes Bengaluru.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to the impact of the accident, the deceased D.Teja sustained grievous injuries.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the Truck vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-31-TF-7119.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 18 years.
According to the petitioners deceased D.Teja was Cleaner and he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.
19. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
20.
22. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was M. Venkatappa vs Janardhan Bajantrhi on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167242104/
6 between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."
Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged below 40 years and therefore 40% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, Since the deceased was bachelor 50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses of the deceased.
As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 18.
As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
25. Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.
26. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 is the owner and 2 is the insurer of the vehicle in which the deceased was traveling and Ex.P.7 charge sheet/final report does not reveals any information stating that the said respondent No.1 and 2 are held responsible for the occurrence of alleged accident in this case.
